title: Beth Din misconduct evidence-state baseline — issue #2646
summary: Bounded first pass separating an adjudicated federal get-coercion case from two distinct 2026 New York civil-review records that do not establish misconduct on the merits.

caveats: The pass is intentionally bounded and does not claim issue #2646 is complete.
The 2013 federal case involved a specific ad-hoc beth din convened in Martin Wolmark's office; no connection to Beth Din of America is asserted.
The Redacted v Redacted misconduct allegation was not adjudicated because the proceedings settled and were discontinued.
Mittel was dismissed on arbitral-immunity grounds; that disposition does not adjudicate the merits of misconduct allegations.

data.research_question: What can be established from primary public records about Beth Din misconduct/coercion without conflating distinct tribunals or promoting allegations into findings?
data.method: Bounded primary-source pass using U.S. Department of Justice charging/sentencing records, official New York court opinions, and Beth Din of America first-party rules; packet created outside db/ for canonical import/merge validation.

findings.finding: PROVEN/ADJUDICATED: Martin Wolmark pleaded guilty to conspiracy to travel in interstate commerce to commit extortion and received a 38-month sentence. Official records state that Wolmark, Mendel Epstein, and Jay Goldstein convened an ad-hoc beth din in Wolmark's office on October 2, 2013 as part of the planned forced-get operation.

PROVEN/ADJUDICATED: Mendel Epstein was convicted at trial of conspiracy to commit kidnapping and sentenced to 120 months; Binyamin Stimler was convicted of conspiracy and attempted kidnapping and sentenced to 39 months. These convictions corroborate the criminal coercion scheme, but they do not identify the ad-hoc beth din as Beth Din of America.

ALLEGED / NOT ADJUDICATED: In Matter of Redacted v Redacted, a husband sought to vacate a Beth Din of America award alleging irrationality and refusal to hear evidence. The proceedings settled and were discontinued in October 2025, so the cited opinion records the allegation but does not decide it.

PROCEDURAL / NOT A MISCONDUCT MERITS FINDING: In Mittel v The Beth Din of the United States of America, Inc., the First Department affirmed dismissal because agreed rules conferred arbitral immunity. The exact organization is kept separate from Beth Din of America pending evidence resolving any relationship.

INSTITUTIONAL BASELINE: Beth Din of America currently publishes rules/procedures for its arbitration proceedings; that first-party policy is useful for later governance comparison but is not itself evidence that procedures were followed or violated in any particular case.
